submitted.rationale: Index 1 (Ca0.14 Fe0.70 Mn0.16, the most Fe-rich spot) gave the only non-zero photocurrent (1e-8 A) of the three measurements. That fits a hematite-like phase absorbing 2.4 eV light: MEGNet puts the Fe2O3 gap between 1.5 eV (PBE) and 2.8 eV (HSE), and MACE puts it on the hull.

rejected.reason: Ca-rich (Ca 0.50, Fe 0.35) region measured about 0 A
Fe-rich with lower Mn and higher Ca measured about 0 A; Ca 0.22 seems to hurt more than lower Mn helps

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gap for hematite Fe2O3 (mp-19770) is ~2.8 eV (HSE overestimates; experimental ~2.1 eV), close to/below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so the most Fe-rich (hematite-like) compositions are the best bet to absorb and give photocurrent. Index 1 is the most Fe-rich candidate.

Uninformative-to-mild: MACE confirms hematite is on the hull, but the most Fe-rich spot (idx 1) gave only 1e-8 A, so the hematite-dominated region looks weak. I'm diversifying to the Ca-rich side (idx 74, Ca 0.50/Fe 0.35), where Ca2Fe2O5-type phases with a smaller gap may form.

Support: the Fe2O3 gap bracket (PBE 1.5 eV / HSE 2.8 eV, so about 2.1 eV experimentally) sits below 2.4 eV, so hematite-rich films absorb. The Fe-rich region gave the only non-zero signal so far, and the Ca-rich region gave zero. Index 4 has the lowest Mn (0.12) among the Fe-rich spots, which should reduce Mn-related recombination.
